# Debrief: Istio, Envoy

These clips cover Istio and Envoy in practice: ambient mesh resource savings and migration friction, Envoy defaults that surprised teams moving off ingress-nginx, and Istio's architecture and upgrade history. ([The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 9:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=587s); [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s); [Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s))

## Top 3 takeaways

1. Moving to Envoy changed behavior: shared, reused upstream connections let long requests block short ones on synchronous services, and encoded slashes were unescaped, causing 404s. Zapier fixed both with explicit settings. ([From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))
2. Dropping sidecars for Istio ambient cut mesh proxy resource allocation by an estimated 40-60% and reduced version drift, but cert-manager and Argo Rollouts needed Gateway API changes or plugins. ([The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 9:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=587s); [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s))
3. Sidecars required restarting every pod to upgrade, and it was hard to see which pods had which version. Istio introduced ztunnel, a per-node L4 proxy for mTLS, and supports parallel Istiod versions for canary upgrades. ([Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s))

## Action items

- [ ] If you run synchronous backends behind Envoy, test whether long requests delay short ones on reused connections, and consider one request per connection in circuit breaker settings, accepting the efficiency tradeoff. ([From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))
- [ ] Check whether apps like Argo CD or Vault depend on percent-encoded paths, and review Envoy's path normalization settings, weighing the security implications of disabling normalization. ([From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s))
- [ ] Before evaluating ambient mode, list tooling such as cert-manager and Argo Rollouts that may need experimental features or Gateway API plugins, and measure your current sidecar resource allocation as a baseline. ([The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s); [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 9:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=587s))

## Watch together (11 min)

1. [From ingress-nginx to Envoy Gateway at Zapier: The Benefits, Challenges, and Migration Lessons That Matter · 8:51](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kIj2U13VZJY&t=531s) (3:38), Kalen Wessel: Concrete Envoy default pitfalls and fixes seen in production.
2. [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 9:47](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=587s) (1:23), Alfonso Ming, Jorge Turrado: Measured ambient savings versus sidecars and reduced version drift.
3. [The Good, The Ugly, and The Bad: Leaving Sidecars Behind with Istio Ambient Mesh · 21:59](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ToKv7JntLvY&t=1319s) (1:21), Alfonso Ming, Jorge Turrado: Tooling friction when adopting ambient and Gateway API.
4. [Evolution or Revolution: Istio as the Network Platform for Cloud Native · 4:24](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4K6s5y8HoBc&t=264s) (1:25), Mitch Connors, Daniel Grimm: Explains why Istio moved from sidecars to ztunnel.
5. [Zero-Downtime Migration from ingress-nginx to Istio in a Multi-Cluster Kubernetes Platform at Bloomberg · 14:20](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wix_PfQ61jY&t=860s) (3:37), Joe Abellard: Compares migration strategies for zero-downtime move to Envoy ingress.
